title: Remote Conveyancing Paralegal
company: LEGAL TALENT PARTNERS LIMITED - Agency - Permanent
description:
Remote Conveyancing Paralegal

£30,000-40,000

Quality. Technology. Flexibility. A Better Way to Do Conveyancing.

We're partnering with a fast-growing, forward-thinking residential conveyancing firm that is using technology, smarter processes and a collaborative team structure to change the way property law is delivered.

The firm is built around a simple idea: conveyancing should be simpler, clearer and faster - for clients and the people delivering it.

If you're an experienced conveyancing paralegal looking for greater autonomy, better technology, a sustainable workload and the flexibility of a fully remote role, this could be an excellent next move.

Why This Role Stands Out

This is not a traditional conveyancing environment where paralegals are left to manage overwhelming caseloads with little support.

You'll work within small, collaborative teams, with regular check-ins, structured 1-to-1s, feedback and personalised training.

The firm takes a quality over quantity approach to workload, maintaining sustainable caseloads and giving teams capacity to deal with peaks without compromising client service.

You'll benefit from:
- Sustainable caseloads and a strong focus on work-life balance
- Small, collaborative teams
- Regular support, feedback and development
- Bespoke technology designed around legal teams
- A culture where asking for help is encouraged
- The opportunity to influence how technology and processes develop
- Fully remote working with genuine flexibility

The result? A more manageable workload, better support and the freedom to focus on delivering excellent conveyancing rather than simply processing as many files as possible.

The Role

As a Conveyancing Paralegal, you'll be an integral part of a residential conveyancing team, working alongside lawyers and other paralegals to deliver an excellent client service.

You'll work across freehold and leasehold sales, purchases and remortgages, taking ownership of your matters while working collaboratively with the wider team.

Your responsibilities will include:
- Progressing residential sales, purchases and remortgages
- Handling freehold sales with minimal supervision
- Managing most leasehold sale enquiries with minimal supervision
- Managing most freehold purchase enquiries with minimal supervision
- Liaising with clients, solicitors, estate agents and other third parties
- Proactively identifying issues and keeping transactions moving
- Reviewing and responding to enquiries
- Maintaining clear, jargon-free communication
- Using the firm's technology to manage your caseload efficiently
- Identifying and resolving potential issues before they become blockers
- Providing feedback to improve systems and processes

The firm's technology has been developed specifically around its conveyancing process, and legal professionals are encouraged to provide feedback on the tools they use every day.

About you

You'll ideally have:
- Strong experience in residential conveyancing
- Experience handling freehold sales with limited supervision
- Experience dealing with leasehold sale enquiries
- Experience dealing with freehold purchase enquiries
- Confidence communicating with clients and third parties
- A proactive approach to progressing transactions
- Strong organisation and attention to detail
- Excellent communication and problem-solving skills
- Confidence working independently in a remote environment
- An interest in using technology to improve legal work

You don't need to be qualified. This role is suited to an experienced paralegal with strong technical conveyancing skills who is ready to take greater ownership of their work.

Although fully remote, you won't be left alone with a laptop and a pile of files. Regular team check-ins, 1-to-1s and ongoing feedback are built into the firm's approach.

The Culture:

This is a firm deliberately doing things differently.

Rather than chasing maximum utilisation, it takes a sustainable approach to workload, helping teams maintain consistent service levels while giving people room to deal with the unexpected.

Its technology helps allocate work, streamline processes and keep teams informed, while its remote-working model is built around communication, supervision, feedback and development.

There's also a strong culture of transparency and continuous improvement. People are encouraged to share ideas, challenge processes and help shape the future of the business.

The Package
- £30,000-£40,000 depending on experience
- Fully remote - work from anywhere in the UK
- Flexible working hours
- 25 days' holiday + 3 days at Christmas + Bank Holidays
- Full home-working setup and equipment provided
- Comprehensive private healthcare
- Free access to Spill mental health and wellbeing support
- Company pension scheme
- Enhanced maternity, paternity and adoption leave
- Growth Shares, giving employees an opportunity to share in the long-term success of the business
- Fully paid-for annual company weekend
- Structured development and genuine progression opportunities

The firm's flexible approach is a key part of its culture, with many employees working flexible hours or part-time. The focus is on creating working patterns that work for both the individual and the wider team.

If you're an experienced conveyancing paralegal looking for a genuinely modern, supportive and flexible place to build your career, we'd love to hear from you.

title: Receptionist
description: The ideal candidate will have strong communication skills, the ability to prioritise and multitask, as well as demonstrable administrative experience. We use a variety of different systems, so being confident in IT and with the ability to pick new things up quickly would be advantageous. You will be joining a fast-paced and changing environment using a range of clinical systems and Microsoft packages. A working knowledge of Microsoft Office packages, including Word, Excel and Outlook will be essential. Knowledge of the Trust systems such as eCare, ESR and Open Eyes would be an advantage, however training would be given in respect to any training needs. You should have a flexible approach to working hours and duties and the ability to think creatively. Experience of working to deadlines, on your own initiative and maintaining strict confidentiality are also essential. Sometimes we are contacted by individuals who may be distressed or upset, the ability to deal with such situations confidently and sensitively is vital. Working as part of the reception team you will be responsible for greeting patients at reception, checking and updating personal details while maintaining patient confidentiality. Using ESR and other relevant booking systems you will arrange follow-up appointments and update details accurately and efficiently. You'll have excellent communication skills and will deal appropriately with enquires both by telephone and in person. Please see job description for full details. To develop and maintain effective working relationships with all Trust staff including clinicians, nursing staff and medical secretaries to provide an accurate, efficient, professional and seamless service to patients and visitors. To ensure patient case notes and clinic lists are available before the commencement of the clinic. To check patient details are correct and amend or update details on the appropriate Patient System and in case notes, when necessary, in accordance with standards set by Information Governance. Reception Function: To greet every patient in a pleasant, professional and calm manner, directing the patient to the appropriate area. To encourage patients in a polite manner to use self-check in machines where applicable, assisting as appropriate. To deal with patients in a polite and respectful manner complying with their requests where possible and where it is not possible to deal with them with dignity and respect. To be responsible for placing patients on the outpatient follow up waiting lists, for making follow up appointments ensuring effective and efficient use of all clinic slots and to ensure that all patients data is recorded accurately. To ensure that clinic outcomes, including attendance, DNAs and their pathway status. To adhere to the Trust Access Policy To assist with changes to workflows with new systems implemented. To liaise closely with Patient Appointment Centre (PAC) to ensure effective communication with regards to the appointments system. To be able to prioritise and demonstrate good time management. To complete any administrative duties to a high standard as required, taking, recording and acting upon telephone messages and requests in a polite and helpful manner.

title: Administrative Assistant
description: Woolpit Health Centre has an exciting opportunity for an Administrative Assistant to join our friendly and supportive Administration Team. We are looking for someone who is enthusiastic, reliable and organised, with a willingness to learn and develop their skills. This role would suit someone who is new to administration and looking to start a career in healthcare, as well as someone with previous administrative or healthcare experience who is looking for their next opportunity. Previous experience within a GP practice or healthcare setting would be beneficial but is not essential, as full training and support will be provided to the right candidate. The successful applicant will assist with a range of administrative tasks to support the smooth day-to-day running of the Health Centre. We are looking for someone who is: Friendly, approachable and professional Well organised and able to manage a variety of tasks Reliable and willing to learn new skills Able to work accurately with good attention to detail Comfortable working both independently and as part of a team Flexible and adaptable in responding to the needs of the Practice Committed to providing a high standard of service to patients and colleagues The role will involve providing general administrative support to the Practice and its staff, as directed by the Administration Lead. Manage patient, healthcare professional and third-party enquiries via email, telephone and face-to-face. Process clinical records, correspondence, pathology results and workflow tasks accurately and efficiently. Scan, uploaded, code and allocate clinical documentation for GP review and maintain accurate patient records. Manage patient registrations and medical records through Healthtech-1. Support reception and clinical teams with Anima online requests and administrative workflows. Support QOF targets by contacting patients regarding annual health reviews and appointments. Maintain patient confidentiality and comply with NHS policies, procedures and data protection requirements. Undertake general administrative duties and provide additional support to the management and GP team as required. General Administrative Duties Monitor the practice generic email inbox, responding to enquiries from patients, healthcare professionals, and third parties in a timely and professional manner. Process and transfer clinical records accurately, allocating documents to appropriate clinical workflows for GP review. Scan, upload and code clinical correspondence onto the patient clinical system while maintaining accurate healthcare records. Distribute daily pathology and laboratory results to clinicians for review through the clinical system. Monitor and action tasks within clinical and workflow systems efficiently to support smooth practice operations. Process and manage administrative and clinical correspondence through the Anima workflow system. Handle patient, staff, and healthcare professional enquiries effectively, both face-to-face and over the telephone. Answer incoming calls, transferred calls appropriately, and resolved queries in a professional and confidential manner. Register and process new patient registrations through the Healthtech-1 portal, including medical records and deductions. Carry out general administrative duties including scanning, photocopying, filing, and document management. Support the delivery of QOF (Quality Outcomes Framework) targets by contacting patients regarding annual health reviews and appointments. To support the reception team with processing online requests via Anima alongside the duty GPs Maintain confidentiality and adhere to practice protocols to ensure consistent, high-quality patient care and compliance with NHS procedures. Undertake additional duties as required by the Practice Manager, Operations Manager, Administration Lead, or the GP team.

title: Practice Administrator
description: As healthcare shifts closer to the community, High Street Surgery is evolving to meet the needs of our growing local population. To support our upcoming practice expansion plans, improve operational efficiency, and further support our dedicated team, we are thrilled to be increasing our workforce across both clinical and administrative roles. We are seeking a passionate and dynamic person to join us, someone who wants to support high-quality care and grow their career alongside a progressive, forward-thinking GP practice. The role of the Practice Administrator is designed to assist the management team with the day-to-day administration of the practice. The primary focus is to support the delivery of key targets,QOF,vaccination programmes,CQC searches, and clinical coding. Providing administrative support practice-wide and spanning across multiple teams, the role ensures effective communication, seamless collaboration, and the delivery of a high-quality service to both the practice and its patients. DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILTIES Maintain smear and recall registers. Have an oversight of the baby immunisation achievement, encouraging parents to bring their child in for vaccinations within the required timeframe. Keep databases up to date and relevant. Support vaccination programs to achieve positive outcomes Monitor and manage the CQC searches. Support the Practice Manager and Deputy Practice Manager to keep policies and protocols up to date. Ensure supplies of necessary refreshments/sundries are maintained. Practice shopping as required. Support the Audit process To monitor and review clinical coding in the practice. To monitor and support the delivery of QOF, highlighting any areas of under achievement to the Practice Manager To take meeting minutes as and when required Support all IT requirements in the practice, liaising with external providers. Support reception team and be able to undertake reception duties as required. Support secretarial team and be able to undertake duties as required. Take post to post office as required. To execute any other duties that may be required under the remit of this role to support the needs of the business. COMMUNICATION The post-holder should recognise the importance of effective communication within the team and will strive to: Communicate effectively with other team members. Communicate effectively with patients and carers. Recognise peoples needs for alternative methods of communication and respond accordingly. DELIVERING A QUALITY SERVICE The post-holder will strive to maintain quality within the Practice, and will: Alert other team members to issues of quality and risk. Assess own performance and take accountability for own actions, either directly or under supervision Contribute to the effectiveness of the team by reflecting on own and team activities and making suggestions on ways to improve and enhance the teams performance. Work effectively with individuals in other agencies to meet patients needs. Effectively manage own time, workload and resources. MANAGEMENT OF RISK Manage and assess risk within the areas of responsibility, ensuring adequate measures are in place to protect staff and patients Monitor work areas and practices to ensure they are safe and free from hazards and conform to health, safety and security legislation, policies, procedures and guidelines Apply infection-control measures within the practice according to local and national guidelines Advocate for policies that reduce environmental health risks, are culturally sensitive and increase access to health care for all MANAGING INFORMATION Use technology and appropriate software as an aid to management in planning, implementation and monitoring of care, presenting and communicating information Review and process data using accurate Read codes in order to ensure easy and accurate information retrieval for monitoring and audit processes Manage information searches using the internet and local library databases Understand responsibility of self and others to the practice and primary care trust regarding the Freedom of Information Act LEARNING AND DEVELOPMENT Assess own learning needs and undertake learning as appropriate Provide an educational role to patients, carers, families, and colleagues in an environment that facilitates learning EQUALITY AND DIVERSITY Identify patterns of discrimination and take action to overcome this and promote diversity and equality of opportunity Enable others to promote equality and diversity in a non-discriminatory culture Support people who need assistance in exercising their rights Monitor and evaluate adherence to local chaperoning policies Act as a role model in the observance of equality and diversity good practice Accept the rights of individuals to choose their care providers, participate in care and refuse care Assist patients from marginalised groups to access quality care Undertake training required to meet the needs of the practice Scope and Purpose of Job Description The job description does not constitute a term and condition of employment. It is provided only as a guide to assist the employee in the performance of their job. The practice is a fast-moving organisation and therefore changes in employees duties may be necessary from time to time. The job description is not intended to be an inflexible or finite list of tasks and may be varied from time to time after consultation/discussion with the post holder. Other Information: General The duties of this post are a guide to the range of responsibilities that may be required. These may change from time to time to meet the needs of the service and/or the development needs of the post holder. This job description will be revised regularly to take account of changes within the organisational structure and the practice business plan. Other duties The post holder will be required to undertake any other duties according to the needs of the service. This job description is not intended to be an exhaustive list of activities, but rather an outline of the main areas of responsibility. Any reasonable changes will be discussed and agreed with the post holder before any variations to the job description are made. Travel to other sites The post holder may be required to travel. Medical Examinations All appointments are conditional upon prior health clearance by the practice. Failure to provide continuing satisfactory evidence will be regarded as a breach of contract. Professional Registration Staff undertaking work which requires professional/state registration are responsible for ensuring that they are so registered and that they comply with any Codes of Conduct applicable to that profession. Proof of registration must be produced on appointment and, if renewable, proof of renewal must also be produced. Disclosure and Barring Service Check This post is subject to the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act (Exceptions Order) 1975 and as such it will be necessary for a submission for Disclosure to be made to the Disclosure and Barring Service (formerly known as CRB) to check for any previous criminal convictions. Equal Opportunities The post-holder will support the equality, diversity and rights of patients, carers, and colleagues, to include: Acting in a way that recognises the importance of peoples rights, interpreting them in a way that is consistent with practice procedures and policies, and current legislation. Respecting the privacy, dignity, needs and beliefs of patients, carers, and colleagues. Work Visa/ Permits/Leave to Remain If you are a non-resident of the United Kingdom or European Economic Union, you are required to have a valid work visa and leave to remain in the UK, which is renewed as required. We offer Tier 2 sponsorship for the right candidate. Code of Conduct All staff are required to work in accordance with the code of conduct for their professional group (e.g., Nursing and Midwifery Council, Health Professions Council, General Medical Council, NHS Code of Conduct for Senior Managers). Confidentiality All information obtained during the post holders duties should be treated as strictly confidential. Any breach of confidence or disclosure of such information, without express permission, may lead to disciplinary action. The post holder has a responsibility to comply with the Data Protection Act 1998, Access to Health Records Act (1990) and Code of Practice on Confidentiality. Health and Safety at Work The post holder is required to take responsible care for the health and safety of him/herself and other persons who may be affected by his/her acts or omissions at work. The post holder is also required to ensure that statutory and practice safety regulations are adhered to. Health and Safety at Work Act 1974 Infection control It is the responsibility of all staff, whether clinical or non-clinical, to familiarise themselves with and adhere to current policy in relation to the prevention of the spread of infection. Complaints From time to time, complaints may occur, no matter how professional the approach of our staff. All complaints are investigated promptly, and the full co-operation of staff is required. The current guidelines amplify the above points with policies and procedures explained. Clinical Governance and Risk management The Practice believes everyone has a role to play in improving and contributing to the quality of care provided to our patients. As an employee of the practice, you are expected to take a proactive role in supporting the Practices clinical governance agenda by: Taking part in activities for improving quality such as clinical audit Identifying and managing risks through incident and near miss reporting and undertaking risk assessments Following polices, guidelines and procedures Maintaining continued professional development Clinical staff making entries into patient health records are required to follow any Practice standards of record keeping Information Quality Assurance As an employee of the Practice, it is expected that you will take due diligence and care in regard to any information collected, recorded, processed, or handled by you during the course of your work and that such information is collected, recorded, processed and handled in compliance with Practice requirements and instructions. Freedom of Information The post holder should be aware of the responsibility placed on employees under the Freedom of Information Act 2000 and is responsible for helping to ensure that the Practice complies with the Act when handling or dealing with any information relating to Practice activity.

title: GP Receptionist
description: We are looking for a Part time member of staff to cover approx. 20 hours per week, with some weekend working. This is an exciting role that will include working within our reception. The role is very varied with every day being different. Your role is important to make sure that patients will be receiving the very best of care that they expect. Full support and training will be given. Prospective applicants are welcome to contact the Deputy Practice Manager, Abby Lake for an informal visit or further information. This position is not available to those that live overseas or require sponsorship to work in the UK. Good communication skills are essential.The role includes communicating with patients and colleagues, either face to face, via the telephone, sending texts, typing letters or emails. You will be Flexible and the ability to organise your time is important to the role. You will be working in our reception area dealing with patients within the surgery, with repeat prescription requests, the administration of medical reports or general queries. Scanning and clinically coding letters from other clinical settings, arranging to call patients for their regular chronic illness checks or managing our e-consultation system. You will be organised and work to efficient systems. You may be typing and organising the referrals to different organisations. You will be able to work within a team but also under your own initiative. To receive and book in patient's for Nurses and Doctors. To make appointments for patients. Answer telephone and deal with any resulting enquiries/requests. Accept and action all requests for repeat prescriptions whether requested in person, by e-mail, by fax or by post. To extract medical records for appointments, telephone messages, prescriptions etc. Complete the necessary documentation for temporary residents, immediate necessary treatment and emergency treatment. Charge and collect all private fees for non contracted work. Filing of various documents as required. Receive transport requests from patients and action them according to Surgery policy. Action on a daily basis any requests for home visits. Take messages for the District Nurses. Deal with incoming/outgoing post. Make tea/coffee for Doctors/Staff as required. Keep the reception area neat and tidy. Keep Doctors consulting rooms neat and tidy and clear of medical records and prescriptions that have been completed. Lock away prescriptions, make sure the surgery is as clear of filing as possible in the time allowed, ready for the morning staff. Set alarm if building is empty; lock doors and windows. Electronic summarising of patient medical records Scanning of documents into electronic patient records Typing letters either dictated by clinicians or under own discretion Dealing with emails/e-consultations by using strict protocols to signpost patient to the correct place. Adhere fully to the practice confidentiality and safeguarding policies. Undertake any other duties as may be determined from time to time commensurate with the job role.
